main_text.p: pit á medio, ibique primum sæpe comprehendit, postremû deniq; incerto aliquo & inopinato casu cõcludit. Sic (ut Horatius ait) Homerʾ Iliada disposuit: 5Nec gemino bellû Trojanû orditur ab ovo: Semper ad eventû festinat, & in medias res, Non secús ac notas, auditorem rapit: & quæ Desperat tractata nitescere posse, relinquit: Atque ita mentitur, sic veris falsa remiscet, 10 Primo ne medium, medio ne discrepet imum.

Sic Virgilius Aeneam á Sicilia excepit, & in cõvivio Carthaginis, præterita narrante fecit: postrema variis perturbata 15 casib. induxit. Sic comici poetę, tametsi magno cõsilio judicioque, comœdias per actus, scenas, officia personarum distinguunt: efficiunt tamẽ, ut omnia fortuita & inopinata videantur. Oratores veró in civilibus caussis ad victoriâ omnia referunt. Itaque non tam docẽdi, quám permovendi gratiá, firmissimum quodq; primum ab iis collocatur: dum tamen ea quæ æquè excellent, servent-tur etiâ ad extremum, & Homerica dispositione, mediocria in mediâ turbam atque in gregem conferantur. 30
Hæc igitur] Epilogus est methodicę regulę ha stenus

page.notes: Line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 are marginal line markers at right of the text, placed beside lines of the column. Note: the "20" and "25" markers sit beside their lines in the column. Several words in the Homeric and Virgilian verse lines are set in italic. The foot line is a note under the text, partly in italic. Handwriting along the right binding edge is not transcribed. Tail of the foot line ("stenus") is the catchword-like word at the right.
